summary: Analysis block, no computation. The null-set transfer lemma is VALID. If Z satisfies 'for every finite F there is t with (F+t) cap Z = empty' (implied by Z null, with a conull set of good t) and C\Z has a proper k-colouring, then chi(R^2) <= k: each finite configuration is translated off Z and inherits a colouring, so every finite subgraph is k-colourable, and de Bruijn-Erdos/Tychonoff finishes (machine-checked as exists_properColoring_of_finset). A single global translate would need Z empty, so compactness is essential. Necessity: Z = C with k = 1 is a counterexample. Applied to the honeycomb skeleton B: C\B is the disjoint union of cell interiors, so a colouring of it is a cell assignment. Proved: cell-constant gamma is proper on C\B iff diam(C) <= 1 and gamma separates the STRICT pairs dmin < 1 < dmax only; tangency edges impose nothing. Hence a SAT periodic quotient (all cells) gives chi(R^2) <= 6 outright, while a SAT finite patch suffices for nothing (a graph of larger diameter cannot be translated into it). The blanket requirement that boundary ownership precede any upper-bound consequence is WITHDRAWN (banners in CELL-NOGO-v2.md, RECOVERY.md). Asymmetry: UNSAT says nothing, SAT gives the full bound.

verified_results.statement: Lemma (null-set transfer): if Z satisfies (H) 'for every finite F there is t with (F+t) cap Z = empty' and c is a proper k-colouring of C\Z, then chi(R^2) <= k.
verified_results.grade: PROOF (elementary, three steps); Step 3 is Tychonoff/de Bruijn-Erdos in ZFC, the only use of choice

verified_results.statement: (H) holds whenever Z is Lebesgue-null, and the set of good translations is conull (finite union of null sets is null). Null is the operative hypothesis: it also holds for Z = Q^2, so neither closedness nor thinness is needed.
(H) is necessary: with k = 1 and Z = C the hypothesis of properness holds vacuously (C\Z is empty) but the conclusion chi(R^2) <= 1 is false ({0,1} is a unit edge).

Applied to the honeycomb skeleton B (null, countable union of closed segments): a proper 6-colouring of C\B implies chi(R^2) <= 6. C\B equals the disjoint union of all cell interiors, so such a colouring is exactly an assignment of colours to cells constant on interiors.

Equivalence: a cell-constant gamma with k >= 2 is proper on C\B iff (i) diam(C) <= 1 (2a <= 1 for hexagons; a = 1/2 admissible since the interior distance set is then (0,1)) and (ii) gamma separates every pair with dmin < 1 < dmax strictly. Hence the constraint graph is exactly Cay(Z^2, F_strict), the one used by every certificate in this directory.
verified_results.grade: PROOF (uses the interval-image fact of CELL-NOGO-v2.md Lemma 1(1), whose endpoint behaviour was certified computationally earlier)

verified_results.statement: Non-strict tangency edges (dmin = 1 or dmax = 1) impose no constraint, since their unit pairs lie only on the uncoloured skeleton; the weak closed-cell criterion would over-constrain. At a = 1/5 this is ring 3 (N = 3, dmax = 1). Our certificates already use the strict graph, so nothing needs re-deriving.
verified_results.grade: PROOF + consistency check against existing certificates

verified_results.statement: Distinction: a colouring of ALL cells (e.g. a genuinely SAT periodic quotient, which colours every coset) gives chi(R^2) <= 6 outright; a SAT colouring of one finite patch gives nothing, because Step 1 needs F+t inside the coloured region and unit-distance graphs of arbitrarily large diameter exist. Same objection applies to a strip or half-plane.

Asymmetry: an UNSAT (family-exclusion) result says nothing about chi(R^2), but a SAT result would give the full upper bound. So the honeycomb family is a SUFFICIENT (not necessary) family for chi(R^2) <= 6.
REPAIR: the earlier blanket requirement that boundary ownership must be constructed before any 6-upper-bound consequence is withdrawn; banners inserted in CELL-NOGO-v2.md (section 1) and RECOVERY.md.

Existing tree already contains both halves, wired for the LOWER bound: Converse.lean exists_properColoring_of_finset (the compactness step, at full generality) and NullSetRobust.lean not_proper_five_coloring_compl_null, whose proof contains the translate-off-the-null-set step contrapositively. The lemma is those two re-assembled with the contradiction removed and Fin 5 replaced by Fin k.

verified_results.statement: No numerical bound on chi(R^2) is established or changed by this block. There is no positive 6-colouring candidate, and the certificates in this directory exclude a in (1/sqrt28, 1/2].

conjectures: The only range where the honeycomb family can now yield a positive result is a <= 1/sqrt28; by the transfer lemma such a colouring would settle chi(R^2) <= 6, which is why that sliver is worth a search despite the thinning graph there.

Because (H) holds for any null Z, the lemma also says chi(R^2) = chi(R^2 \ Z) for null Z in both directions; the lower direction is already machine-checked (T2), so the pair together says the chromatic number is null-set invariant.
